sources.citation: Rezai Baghbidi, Hassan. 1383 [2004]. Guyeš-e Vidari [The Vidari dialect]. Guyeš-šenāsi (Vīže-nāme-ye Nāme-ye Farhangestān) 1(3): 20-38.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Section 1 'Nezām-e āvāyi' (pp.22-23) treats historical NW-Iranian sound changes, then '1-2 the vowels of Vidari do not differ from standard Persian', '1-3.. has /γ/ in addition to the Persian consonants; [xʷ] heard in some words'. No paragraph on تکیه/stress anywhere in the 19 pages (Persian scanned a full-text search for stress/accent + visual check of the phonology pages).

sources.citation: Yarshater, Ehsan. 1985/1989. ALVĪRĪ. Encyclopaedia Iranica, vol. I, fasc. 9, p. 916.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Phonology paragraph lists consonants/vowels/vowel harmony only. Morphology: 'The common indicator of the feminine gender is an unstressed -a'; 'stressed ba- (or be-, depending on its environment) for the imperative, the subjunctive and the preterite; unstressed be- for the imperfect'. No word-stress position rule.

sources.citation: Stilo, Donald L. 1981. The Tati language group in the sociolinguistic context of Northwestern Iran and Transcaucasia. Iranian Studies 14(3/4): 137-187.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Classificatory/sociolinguistic survey; lists Alviri/Vidari as Group Eight of Tati; a full-text search for stress/accent found nothing phonological.

sources.citation: Yarshater, Ehsan. 1964. The dialects of Alvir and Vidar. In G. Redard (ed.), Indo-Iranica: Mélanges présentés à Georg Morgenstierne à l'occasion de son soixante-dixième anniversaire, 177-187. Wiesbaden: Harrassowitz.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: held in print at Harvard (Widener Library, call number 3260.12); the library holds the journal volume but the item itself was not found; ask your own library for a scan or interlibrary loan
sources.note: Phonology section (p.178) gives no stress rule: 'The phonology of Alviri and Vidari offers no particular interest; it follows the Esh(tehārdi) pattern in general.' Only morpheme-level remarks: p.179 'The common indicator of the fem. gender is an unstressed -a'; p.182 'stressed ba-, be- for the Imperative, the Subjunctive and the Preterite; unstressed be- for the Perfect'; fn.34 'The vowel may vary owing to assimilation or stress.' Verse texts pp.183-185 carry acute accent marks (metrical, no rule stated).

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: en: 'Alviri consonants are the same as those of Persian' only; fa: stub, no phonology. No stress info. en article supplied the archive.org link to the Yarshater 1964 scan.

sources.citation: Izadifar, Rāhele. n.d. «الویری» [Alviri]. Dānešnāme-ye zabānhā va guyešhā-ye Irāni, Markaz-e Dā'erat-ol-ma'āref-e Bozorg-e Eslāmi (CGIE), article 274167.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: 'ویژگیهای آوایی' section repeats Yarshater (consonants = Persian; vowels â u ü o ö a e ë i; vowel harmony). Stress mentioned only morphemically: feminine marker 'a- بدون تکیه در پایان واژه' (unstressed final -a) and perfective prefix '-ba و -be تکیه‌بر' (stressed) vs '-be بدون تکیه' for the perfect. No word-stress rule. Bibliography names Hāšemi 1353 PhD and Tulāni 1380 MA thesis.
